purpose: Browser-first navigation hints for an AI gathering flight offers and route topology.

selection_strategy.partial_scope_disposition: partition exact supported and unsupported remainders; retry supported remainder on current source before advancing only unsupported remainder
selection_strategy.runtime_role: issue_required_source_id, enforce typed dispositions, and reject out-of-order results

sources.name: AZair

product_policy.reason: random_loop accepts airport-to-airport flight edges only

browser_notes: Use as an important low-cost-carrier discovery source for Anywhere, flexible-date, multi-origin, and multi-destination searches.
Keep airport-change-by-ground disabled: this product accepts flight edges only.
Regional and carrier coverage can change and is not guaranteed, and browser automation compatibility is not guaranteed.

Treat displayed fares as discovery evidence; confirm the exact itinerary on Google Flights or another suitable current fare source. Use a carrier or seller page only when facts are missing or conflicting, or when the user asks.

sources.name: Google Flights
browser_notes: Use the map, Dates, Price graph, Airports, Best, and Cheapest views when visible.
Google states that results draw on more than 300 partners but may not include every offer.
Treat an exact dated result with visible flight identity, current fare, and included baggage as sufficient final evidence.
Treat booking links as handoffs to partners, not as Google selling the ticket.

sources.name: Kiwi.com
browser_notes: Use for flexible dates, multiple airports, low-cost-carrier inventory, and independently ticketed virtual-interline combinations.
Capture every segment, self-transfer condition, baggage allowance, seller total, and mandatory extra shown for the exact itinerary.
Do not treat a Kiwi search result as market-complete; compare it with other metasearch, OTA, and airline-direct sources.

sources.name: Trip.com / Ctrip
browser_notes: Use current dated results and price calendars for exact seller offers, including platform-specific public or eligibility-gated fares when the user explicitly requests them.
Keep coupons, membership, student, or other eligibility conditions attached only to the exact observed offer; never transfer them to another seller's quote.
Capture displayed baggage, ticket conditions, mandatory fees, and the final payable total before admission.

sources.name: Skyscanner
browser_notes: Use Everywhere, nearby airports, and Flexible dates or whole-month views when available.
Calendar prices may be indicative and based on recent searches; open a date to refresh an offer.
Skyscanner redirects to an airline or travel provider for booking.

sources.name: KAYAK
browser_notes: Use Explore for flexible destinations and plus-or-minus days or month search for flexible dates.
Confirm the final seller and current total before recording an observed offer.

sources.name: FlightConnections
browser_notes: Use for route, airport, airline, direct-flight, stopover, and arrive-here/depart-from-here discovery.
Treat it as topology and schedule discovery; verify any fare through a fare source or carrier.

sources.name: Southwest Airlines
browser_notes: Use the Low Fare Calendar for a known route and the route map for carrier coverage.
Use when the candidate region or a metasearch result indicates Southwest may operate the leg.

sources.name: Frontier Airlines
browser_notes: Use direct search and the official route map after Frontier is identified as a candidate operator.
Record the displayed fare basis and mandatory extras separately.

sources.name: Ryanair
browser_notes: Use Fare Finder and direct search after Ryanair is identified as a candidate operator.
Record the fare bundle and mandatory extras separately.

sources.name: AirAsia
browser_notes: Use AirAsia Flights Only when confirming an AirAsia-operated candidate.
The AirAsia MOVE interface may also show other airlines; preserve the actual operator and seller.

dynamic_source_rule.instruction: Use an operator's official website when it is the most useful source, when another source leaves material facts missing or conflicting, or when the user asks. It is not a mandatory final-verification step.
